note: The material finishing pass for painted characters (scripts/blender/finish_materials.py). The painter gives every surface one kind of paint; this pass gives each material class the surface it is made of: grain, weave, hammering and scratches as relief in a normal map, roughness and metalness that vary the way the material does, worn edges on metal and grime in crevices. Scales are in millimetres on the real-scale character. Detail finer than about 2 mm aliases at a 4096 atlas on a 1.8 m character, so nothing here is finer.

metal.why: Worn iron: hammered faces, fine scratches that catch the light, bright bare metal where edges rub, dark grime where the plate meets what it sits on.

leather.why: Pebbled grain and creases; rubbed areas lighter and smoother, the pores and folds darker and rougher. Leather is never metallic.

cloth.why: A woven surface: threads in two directions, slubs and fuzz, almost no specular. The weave is what tells cloth from painted plastic up close.

skin.why: Pores and a soft sheen; skin is dielectric and only a little glossy.
